dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: The lines here are a bit wooden too. Maybe the writing should better reflect the characters' inner psychology and mentality, the audience should be able to understand this part of the plot...

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: Ah, please refrain, Fourmon. Are you going to obfuscate the dialogue to the point the audience is left guessing again?

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: Do you recall the last performance? Nobody understood any of it! All they could say was "Didn't understand much but seemed very avant-garde!" And we were trying to write a situational comedy...

dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: B—But of course it won't be like the last time...

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: Don't be unreasonable, Fourmon. You need to consider the audience's perspective when you try to decide how to communicate the meaning of the play.

dialogues.speaker: Fourmon
dialogues.text: You're right. Okay, okay, I'll do another edit.

dialogues.speaker: Meilhat
dialogues.text: You'll need to be quick. We have a rehearsal this evening.
